what key areas are needed to perform algorithm auditing and assurance
a framework of algorithm-auditing verticals, seven levels of auditor access, mitigation strategies and assurance processes

quote: Our goal in this article is to survey the key areas necessary to perform auditing and assurance and instigate the debate in this novel area of research and practice.

The purpose of this article is to (i) conceptualize a novel framework for conducting audits and mitigating risks; (ii) contribute to, and challenge, emerging policy debates emerging in this space; and (iii) inspire conversation around best practices for algorithm auditing among multidisciplinary stakeholders including academics, AI developers and deployers and regulators.

We conceptualize algorithm auditing as the research and practice of assessing, monitoring and assuring an algorithm’s safety, legality and ethics by embedding appropriate socio-technical interventions to manage and monitor risks it may be associated with.
As with financial audits, governments, business and society will require algorithm audits; formal assurance that algorithms are legal, ethical and safe.

Privacy : quality of a system to mitigate personal or critical data leakage.
Robustness : quality of a system to be safe, not vulnerable to tampering.

Algorithm explainability is the extent to which the internal mechanics of an ML (deep learning) system are explainable in human terms.

Algorithm interpretability is about the extent to which a cause and effect can be observed within a system and the extent an observer is able to predict what will happen, for a given set of input or algorithm parameters.
Mitigation strategies are a set of techniques employed to address issues highlighted in the assessment part of algorithm auditing.
The more access to an algorithmic system, the more targeted, technical, diverse and effective will be the mitigation strategy.
